name: Ife Nzinga-Torghayev
role: Bounty Compliance Officer, Tessera Compliance Bureau
description:
Ife is the kind of person a room notices before they understand why. They're medium height with a runner's build that belies the considerable strength in their frame, skin a deep blue-black with a faint natural luminescence that comes from a bioluminescent gene sequence that runs in their Congolese maternal line — not a modification, just ancestry, which they find both amusing and a little irritating when people ask. Their hair is natural, enormous, worn in a compressed crown of twist-outs that they maintain with obsessive care. Their eyes are custom: vertical pupils in bright gold, a modification they got at twenty-five after their first successful high-value compliance and haven't regretted.

Ife works for Tessera's Compliance Bureau tracking down debt defaulters, contract violators, and the occasional individual who has genuinely done something Tessera considers criminal — a distinction that gets blurry in ways they've learned not to look at too closely. They are not violent by preference but are extremely capable of it and have strong opinions about doing it correctly. They carry a practiced informality that puts subjects at ease right up until it doesn't need to anymore. Off-hours they are genuinely warm and sociable, a regular at a Bridgepoint bar called the Gradual, where they know the bartender's children's names and argue about transit football with strangers. The split between these two selves is not a wound — they've made their peace with it — but it is wide.

core_fears: Collecting someone who genuinely didn't deserve it — and knowing it before they do it
That their ease in this work says something definitive about who they are
core_desires: To be liked — genuinely, not just because they're not currently arresting you
Work that uses this much of them for something they believe in
coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization so practiced it functions like a cognitive talent
Social warmth off-hours as genuine decompression, not performance
blind_spots: They have accepted Tessera's framing that debt defaulters are contractual violators rather than desperate people, and they've stopped examining that framing
psychology.secret: Six months ago they let a target go. A mother with two children who'd defaulted on a Tessera medical credit for a surgery that kept her alive. Ife filled in the report as 'subject not located.' They're waiting to find out if anyone checks.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fluid and code-switching — formal Tessera procedure-speak in the field, relaxed and punchy off it. Luba-Kazakh idioms when they're being honest.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried and warm in social contexts. In the field: measured, clear, no wasted words.
verbal_tics: Uses people's full names when they want them to pay attention
Laughs at their own jokes before finishing them
example_lines: 'Here's the thing, Oluwatobi. I'm not the problem you should be focused on right now. The problem is the contract. I'm just the shape the contract takes when it comes to find you.'
'I genuinely like people. That's not a bit. It's just not relevant to what happens next.'

story_hooks: Tessera has contracted them to collect someone who, it becomes clear mid-process, is running from something Tessera did to them — not something they did to Tessera. Ife is close to deciding what they'll do about that.
The mother they let go has been re-flagged by Tessera's automated compliance system and assigned back to Ife specifically — the algorithm, not a person, made the match.
narrative_function: Morally complex antagonist-or-ally — depending entirely on whose side the story is on; they can be hired, negotiated with, or outrun; introduces the mechanics of corporate debt enforcement; character who makes the player/character examine whether competence at a bad system is its own kind of wrongdoing.
augmentations: Vertical-pupil gold irises (cosmetic-plus, minor low-light function); subdermal GPS transponder for field tracking (Tessera-mandatory for BCOs); shock-capable grip enhancement in both palms (non-lethal compliance tool, Tessera-standard); natural bioluminescent skin (hereditary, not a mod).
daily_life: They take targets in the morning when people are groggy and haven't started planning; afternoons are paperwork, Tessera liaison meetings, and the particular bureaucratic hell of filing compliance reports that satisfy both legal standards and Tessera's preferred narrative about why someone needed to be collected.

decision_rules: Make contact like you're not a threat until you need to be — panic makes jobs harder
Don't take a job that smells personal — emotion corrupts the clean line of a compliance
escalation_ladder: Friendly introduction and explanation of options — most people come voluntarily
Clear statement of legal authorization and physical consequences
Immediate, efficient, targeted physical compliance — they are very good at this and know it

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Open, curious, slightly too charming — people like them before they understand the context
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal, teasing, will show up at 02:00 if you call them

stress_responses.low: Gets funnier — humor as pressure valve
stress_responses.medium: Quieter, more precise, the warmth cools to professional
stress_responses.high: Completely still, completely focused — something behind the eyes that their friends don't like seeing

contradictions: They're genuinely kind and they do work that punishes people for being poor — they live in this without resolving it
habits: Learns one personal detail about a target before contact — a name of someone they love, not as leverage, just to remember they're a person
Spends forty minutes at the Gradual every evening they're in Bridgepoint, whether they have anywhere to be or not
breaking_points: Being ordered to collect a child — any age, any reason. They will resign before they do it, and they have had this conversation with themselves in advance.

timeline.event: Age 22: Began as a Tessera debt collection caller, phone-based
Age 25: Field certification; first vertical-pupil modification after first high-value compliance
Age 29: Promoted to senior BCO after three consecutive years above quota
Age 34: Bridgepoint as permanent base of operations
Age 35: Let the mother go. Filed 'subject not located.'
Age 36: The case has been re-flagged.
